subject: MSA + Order Form: evidence retention windows, notice timing, and cross-border flags

From: Samuel Price <sam.price@corptech.com>

Cc: CorpTech Legal <legal@corptech.com>

Subject: RE: Draft MSA / Order Form — evidence retention & cross-border flags

Neha — thanks for the updated MSA and order form. A couple quick asks from our side before we route to procurement: 

1) Notice window: your redline currently requires notice 'as soon as reasonably practicable' for a third-party IP claim. We need a hard window (30 days) or we can't provide indemnity on our side.
2) Evidence retention: CorpTech legal wants explicit obligation that Redwood will preserve request/response artifacts for 3 years and provide a searchable bundle on request. Can you confirm whether that is operationally possible (we're okay with a reasonable-cost recovery for export).
3) Cross-border data: our privacy team flagged Order Form section 5.2 — we need explicit notice if evidence is stored outside the EU (we're EU-based for this purchase). If Redwood intends to pull evidence from a US-hosted shard, we need a data transfer addendum and a country-of-storage flag.

I attached our annotated redlines (CorpTech_Indemnity_Redlines_v3.docx). Samuel

--
Samuel Price
Senior Counsel, CorpTech Systems

Subject: RE: Draft MSA / Order Form — evidence retention & cross-border flags

Sam — appreciate the clear asks, good to have them up front. Quick answers and next steps below so we don't lose momentum: 

1) Notice window: we understand the customer's need for certainty. Our legal practice prefers 'as soon as reasonably practicable' because of operational triage, but we can agree to a 30-day notice window in the Order Form for third-party IP claims if coupled with a cooperative evidence handover SLA (see 2). Proposal: 30 days notice + 5 business days to confirm receipt and next steps.

2) Evidence retention: operationally we can preserve request/response logs and relevant KV snapshots for 36 months, subject to export process for non-standard bundles (we'll include a per-request export fee in the SLA). We'll attach the proposed Evidence_Retention_SLA.pdf for redline. Need ops to confirm retention scope (full payload vs metadata).

3) Cross-border storage flags: we can include a country-of-storage disclosure for evidence exports and a data transfer addendum. For EU accounts we can commit to EU-first storage unless customer elects otherwise. Need to confirm with infra whether any inferencing artifacts (cached prefixes) might be routed through a US-hosted pre-warm pool — @rishi can you confirm routing behavior for EU-enterprise tenants?

I've attached our initial redline and the SLA stub. Looping in Kimberly and Rishi to finalize language so we can send back to Sam for counter-redline.

Thanks,
Neha
Neha Kapoor
Manager, Contracts & Procurement

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: RE: Draft MSA / Order Form — evidence retention & cross-border flags

Folks — quick internal notes from legal redlines perspective: 

- We can accept 30-day notice for third-party IP claims but must preserve our right to cure and control defense (standard defend-and-control language). Add explicit 'cooperation' steps to avoid 'notice + blame' problems.
- Evidence retention: 36 months is OK. We should explicitly limit scope to logs and system metadata + customer-submitted content for the claim window. We should push back on an always-on obligation to retain full payloads; that creates storage risk. Suggest wording: 'preserve logs, request/response metadata, and any customer-submitted materials relevant to the claim; provide export with 10 business days notice, subject to reasonable export fee.'
- Cross-border flags: we should offer 'EU-first' storage for EU customers. But do not commit that inferencing cache never transits the US; instead commit to 'no persistent storage of exported evidence outside EU without customer consent' and provide country-of-storage disclosure at time of export. That balances ops constraints.

Neha — I'll draft the specific contract language. Rishi — please confirm the transient routing behavior and whether we can safely represent 'no persistent storage outside EU' for evidence exports.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:32:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RE: Draft MSA / Order Form — evidence retention & cross-border flags

Quick infra confirmation: 

- For EU enterprise customers that opt into EU-first storage, inference artifacts and persisted logs are stored in the EU region. We do maintain transient caches that may exist briefly on pooled US GPUs during cross-region bursts, but those caches are ephemeral (TTL < 2 minutes) and not written to persistent object storage.
- Exported evidence bundles are assembled from EU storage when the account is EU-first by default. If an emergency requires access to a US-hosted backup, we'd surface that to the customer and require consent.

So: we can sign up to 'no persistent storage outside the EU without customer consent' and describe transient cache behavior in plain language. We'll need to ensure the SLA indicates the export window (10 business days) and a limited support window for assembling preserved archives.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Platform Engineering

- 30-day notice window with 5 business days acknowledgement + defence-control preserved per your proposed language.
- 36-month evidence retention scoped to logs, metadata, and customer-submitted artifacts; 10 business days to provide a compiled bundle; export fee acceptable.
- Commitment: 'no persistent storage of exported evidence outside the EU without customer consent' + plain-language disclosure about transient caches.
